_comment: Hawaii 2026 QAP, HHFDC. Competitive scoring is Section III.D, the Criteria Point System, PDF pp.10-20. One criterion per numbered Criterion, which is the grain the plan scores at. Page numbers are PDF page indices; the printed page numbers match. Several criteria are scored relative to the other applications in the round rather than against a fixed standard, which is noted on each.

track_totals.note: The plan states no overall maximum, only a range against each criterion. Summing the stated ranges gives 117 positive points, against which Criterion 23 can deduct up to 2. Note that six criteria are scored relative to the rest of the round, so a project's score is not knowable from the plan alone.

criteria.heading: LIHTC and HHFDC resource efficiency and leveraging
criteria.quote: LIHTC and HHFDC Resource - Efficiency and Leveraging

tiers.tier_label: 1A: HHFDC resources per LIHTC unit, lowest ratio in the round
1B: HHFDC resources over total project cost, lowest ratio in the round

criteria.note: Both halves are scored against the round, not a fixed standard: the lowest ratio takes 5 points, the highest 0, and everything between is proportional. Resources counted are LIHTC, RHRF, DURF and any other permanent financing through HHFDC, with the federal LIHTC request multiplied by 10.

criteria.heading: County adjuster
criteria.quote: County Adjuster
criteria.note: Based on the county's HUD Multifamily Tax Subsidy Project income limit at 60% for a four-person household. The county with the lowest limit takes 2 points, the highest 0, others proportionally, rounded to the nearest hundredth. The plan's worked example uses 2021 limits.

criteria.heading: Reasonableness of development costs
criteria.quote: Reasonableness of Development Costs

tiers.tier_label: Lowest total development cost per residential square foot in the round
Lowest total development cost per unit in the round

criteria.note: Existing buildings already used for housing score zero. The plan gives the formula explicitly: (1 - (subject cost - lowest) / (highest - lowest)) * 6.0. Mixed-use projects with their own non-HHFDC financing may have the non-residential component excluded.

criteria.heading: Applicant's readiness
criteria.quote: Identification of serious issues in need of resolution for the project to proceed

tiers.tier_label: A: project schedule reasonable, no unresolved development or budget issues
B: no discretionary approvals outstanding, including Chapter 343 environmental and land use
C: no ministerial approvals outstanding, drawings complete and under review

criteria.note: Three additive components of 8 each, which is the largest single criterion in the plan.

criteria.heading: Tenant services and amenities
criteria.quote: Tenant services and amenities that will enhance the livability of the project
criteria.note: The plan states no sub-criteria or evidence requirements, so this is judged at HHFDC's discretion.

criteria.heading: Project-based rental assistance subsidies
criteria.quote: Project will be receiving, for the first time, project-based rental assistance subsidies
criteria.note: At least half the units, such that eligible tenants pay about 30% of gross monthly income. Rural Development 515 and HUD programmes are given as examples.

criteria.heading: State or local government financing
criteria.quote: permanent below market loan or grant from a State or local

tiers.tier_label: Commitment of more than $80,000 per unit
Commitment of at least $10,000 but less than $80,000 per unit

criteria.note: From an agency other than HHFDC, evidenced by a commitment letter, government action or contractual agreement.

criteria.heading: State or county government owned land
criteria.quote: The project has received a lease from a State or County government agency
criteria.note: The land must have been government-owned before the application date; property acquired afterwards does not qualify.

criteria.heading: Energy efficiency and green building
criteria.quote: Projects can score points in only one category

tiers.tier_label: LEED Platinum or National Green Building Standard Emerald
Enterprise Green Communities Gold or LEED Gold
Enterprise Green Communities Silver or LEED Silver
EPA Energy Star v3, Enterprise Green Communities Certified, LEED Certified or NGBS Bronze

criteria.note: Electing more than one category forfeits all points in the criterion. An architect's certification that the project can meet the chosen standard is required with the application, and a completion certification afterwards; a missing or inconsistent certification forfeits the points, and failure at completion may forfeit the good faith deposit.

criteria.heading: Project location and market demand
criteria.quote: Located in a County's urban core

tiers.tier_label: Located in a county's urban core
Located in an urbanized area
Located in a master planned community
Rural district near employment, medical and educational facilities
Transit: Oahu rail station or bus stop with 5+ peak buses an hour, neighbour islands 3+, within 0.5 miles
Transit: bus stop of any service frequency within 0.5 miles

criteria.note: A location value plus a transit value, up to the stated maximum of 6. The transit half is the only place in the plan awarding half points.

criteria.heading: Developer and property management experience
criteria.quote: Developer and Property Management Experience

tiers.tier_label: A: development team able to meet all terms and conditions, adjusted for past performance
B: six or more LIHTC projects placed in service by the applicant
C: four or more LIHTC projects placed in service in Hawaii
D: six or more LIHTC projects managed by the management agent
E: four or more LIHTC projects in Hawaii managed by the management agent

criteria.note: Components B to E each award 0.5 at the lower band (1-5 projects, or 1-3 for the Hawaii-specific ones) and 1 at the higher. Component A is discretionary and can be reduced for past performance.

criteria.heading: Length of affordability commitment
criteria.quote: committing to an additional use period beyond the minimum

tiers.tier_label: Perpetuity
61 years or more
55 to 60 years
50 to 54 years
45 to 49 years

criteria.note: The plan contradicts itself and the contradiction is recorded rather than resolved: the criterion heading reads '0 to 7 points' but the table tops out at 6 for perpetual affordability. points_max is set to 6, the highest value actually attainable from the table. Perpetual elections require a funding plan for reserves and capital improvements that does not rely on further HHFDC resources.

criteria.heading: Available and minimum unit sizes
criteria.quote: 20% or more of the total units are 1-bedrooms

tiers.tier_label: Minimum unit sizes met, new construction
20% or more of units are one-bedrooms
20% to 39% of units are two-bedroom or larger
40% or more of units are two-bedroom or larger

criteria.note: Up to 3 for the unit mix plus 2 for meeting minimum sizes: studio 300 sq ft, one-bedroom 360, two 520, three 720, four 880. Measured interior face of wall to interior face of wall, excluding lanais, patios, decks and unattached storage.

criteria.heading: Special housing needs referrals
criteria.quote: Applicants will earn the following points for agreeing to accept referrals

tiers.tier_label: The proposed project and at least one existing project
The proposed project only

criteria.note: Referrals from a state-coordinated system for 10% of units; where referrals are insufficient the owner leases in the regular course. The plan says HHFDC will set further parameters, including the approach to affordability, at a later date.

criteria.heading: Percentage of income targeted units
criteria.quote: Applicants receive points by providing a preference to lower income tenants

tiers.tier_label: Average income at 51%, or 30% of units at 30% AMI
Average income at 54%, or 30% of units at 40% AMI
Average income at 57%, or 30% of units at 50% AMI

criteria.note: The application must reflect one set-aside election, either average income or the original minimum set-aside, and meet the matrix for the election chosen.

criteria.heading: Involvement of a qualified non-profit organisation
criteria.quote: Project involves a Qualified Non-Profit Organization as defined in Section 42
criteria.note: Must own an interest and materially participate throughout the extended use period, elect the non-profit set-aside, hold a physical office in Hawaii, and supply articles of incorporation, a 501(c)(3) letter, the most recent Form 990 and a certificate of vendor compliance.

criteria.heading: Opportunity for home ownership
criteria.quote: Project is offering tenants an opportunity for home ownership
criteria.note: A right of first refusal under section 42(i)(7), with a feasibility analysis of tenants' ability to purchase and a plan for offering the units.

criteria.heading: Qualified census tract with a revitalisation plan
criteria.quote: Project is located in a Qualified Census Tract
criteria.note: Requires redevelopment of existing housing contributing to a concerted community revitalization plan, an explanation of compliance and community benefit, and a letter of interest or binding agreement with the administering agency.

criteria.heading: Historic nature
criteria.quote: The project will preserve the historic nature of an existing building
criteria.note: Buildings on a national or state historic registry.

criteria.heading: Census tracts with concentrated wealth
criteria.quote: based on the percentage of families below the poverty rate in
criteria.note: Scored against the round: the lowest poverty percentage takes the point, the highest takes none, others proportionally. Where a project spans tracts, the highest percentage is used.

criteria.heading: Loan repayment
criteria.quote: full repayment of a Rental Housing Revolving Fund loan
criteria.note: Within the committed RHRF affordability period. Applications not requesting RHRF receive the point automatically.

criteria.heading: State conveyance offer
criteria.quote: agreeing to offer to sell the project to a state agency for fair market
criteria.note: At an appraised fair market value, no later than three years before the end of the extended use period, recorded in the Declaration of Restrictive Covenants.

criteria.heading: Need for rehabilitation
criteria.quote: HHFDC will award between -2 and 0 points based on its determination
criteria.note: Judged on how much the rehabilitation materially improves residents' quality of life, measured as the change between current conditions and the result. New construction receives zero. A criterion that can only subtract.
